judge.governing_law_identified: Conservation of water volume determines the merged radius R=2^(1/3)a; the reduction in liquid-air surface energy is ΔE=γ[2(4πa^2)-4πR^2], and kΔE is equated to the translational kinetic energy Mv^2/2.
judge.regime_assumed: Initially stationary spherical drops of radius a; complete merger into one spherical drop; negligible gravitational-energy change and other losses except that only fraction k of released surface energy becomes jump kinetic energy.
judge.escalate_reason: The result contains the dimensionless geometric factor 2-2^(2/3), arising from the spherical area-volume scaling; it has been independently checked and is correct, but this is a bare geometric factor.

checks_run: dimensional: ΔE=γa^2 has J; v^2=kγ/(ρa) has m^2 s^-2
volume conservation: (4π/3)R^3=2(4π/3)a^3 => R=2^(1/3)a; surface-energy residual ΔE-γ[8πa^2-4πR^2]=0
limiting: k→0 gives v→0; γ→0 gives v→0; a→∞ gives v→0; ΔE>0 since 2>2^(2/3)
root branch: physical jump speed uses positive square root v>0

judge.governing_law_identified: Hydrostatic equilibrium: dP/dz = -rho g, with P(z=0)=P0.
judge.regime_assumed: Static incompressible water of constant density in a uniform gravitational field; z is positive upward.

judge.governing_law_identified: Hydrostatic pressure P=P0-rho g z and integration of the horizontal pressure traction on the cutout water block, per unit y-length.
judge.regime_assumed: Static hydrostatic water, uniform density and gravity, translational invariance along y, with atmospheric pressure contributing zero net horizontal force.
case_branches_found: For the hydrophilic geometry shown, z1>z2, so f_x=(rho g/2)(z2^2-z1^2)<0 when positive x is rightward; the force is therefore leftward.

judge.governing_law_identified: Horizontal force balance on the isolated water block: the pressure-induced horizontal force is balanced by the horizontal components of surface-tension forces at its two free-surface edges.
judge.regime_assumed: Static capillary-hydrostatic equilibrium; uniform surface tension; force per unit length in the y direction; angles measured from the positive x axis as specified.
case_branches_found: For arbitrary left and right edge angles theta1 and theta2, the result is f_x = gamma(cos theta1 - cos theta2).
The formula applies to either raised or depressed interfaces, provided the stated angle convention and corresponding signs of f_x are retained.

judge.governing_law_identified: Static horizontal force balance between hydrostatic pressure and surface-tension forces, yielding the capillary first integral (rho g z^2)/2 + gamma cos(theta) = constant.
judge.regime_assumed: Static two-dimensional water surface, uniform surface tension and density, hydrostatic pressure; no small-slope approximation is used in this sub-part.

checks_run: dimensional: [gamma/(rho*g)]=m^2, so ell=sqrt(gamma/(rho*g)) has length and (z/ell)^a requires a=2
conservation_residual: substituting B.2 fx=(rho*g/2)(z2^2-z1^2) and B.3 fx=gamma(cos(theta1)-cos(theta2)) gives [(rho*g/2)z^2+gamma*cos(theta)]_1=[...]_2=0
limiting_case: at z=0 the first integral reduces to gamma*cos(theta)=constant relative to the far-level reference, consistent with the stated form
BC/root_branch: ell is the positive capillary length sqrt(gamma/(rho*g)); no alternative negative root is physically admissible for a length
symbol_whitelist: uses only rho,g,gamma,z,theta,a,ell and an unspecified dimensionless constant allowed by P
faithfulness_to_P: derives directly from B.2 and B.3 and explicitly remains independent of hydrophilic/hydrophobic branch

judge.governing_law_identified: Linearized capillary-gravity surface-shape equation obtained from the first integral (z^2/(2ℓ^2) + cos θ = constant), with z' = tan θ.
judge.regime_assumed: Small-slope regime |z'(x)| << 1, so cos θ = 1/sqrt(1+z'^2) ≈ 1 - z'^2/2; the far-field surface satisfies z(∞) = 0.
case_branches_found: The growing branch A exp(x/ℓ) is excluded by z(∞) = 0.
The retained decaying branch is z(x) = B exp(-x/ℓ).
The contact-slope condition z'(0) = tan θ0 gives B = -ℓ tan θ0.

conservation residual: for z=-ell*tan(theta0)*exp(-x/ell), z^2/ell^2-z'^2=0 identically and z''-z/ell^2=0
BC/root-branch: z(infinity)=0 eliminates A*exp(x/ell); z'(0)=tan(theta0) fixes B=-ell*tan(theta0)
faithfulness to P: uses the stipulated small-slope approximation, x>=0 domain, and contact angle definition z'(0)=tan(theta0)
symbol-whitelist: final answer uses only z,x,ell,theta0 specified by P; A and B are temporary integration constants

judge.governing_law_identified: Hydrostatic pressure P = P0 - rho g z integrated over the wetted rod boundary, together with the horizontal components of surface-tension forces at the two contact lines.
judge.regime_assumed: Static equilibrium; uniform surface tension; constant-density liquid in a uniform gravitational field; forces are per unit rod length along y; atmospheric-pressure contribution cancels.

judge.governing_law_identified: Hydrostatic pressure together with the capillary first integral (1/2)ρgz^2 + γ cosθ = constant on each connected free-surface segment, combined with the horizontal-force expression from C.1.
judge.regime_assumed: Static equilibrium; identical rod arrangement symmetric about the midpoint between rods; the inner free surface has θ = 0 at the midpoint and the outer free surface approaches z = 0, θ = 0 far from the rods. No small-slope approximation is needed for C.2.

judge.governing_law_identified: The linearized capillary-surface equation from B.5, z'' = z/ell^2, together with left-right symmetry about the midpoint between the rods.
judge.regime_assumed: Small-slope approximation inherited from B.5: |z'(x)| << 1, with the midpoint chosen as x = 0.
case_branches_found: Symmetric interior meniscus: z(x) = z0 cosh(x/ell).
